nodes.name: crankSpin
nodes.coreScript:
-- Crank angle in radians, measured from top dead centre, advanced one step per strobe while this
-- node is animating. Each of the three mechanism transforms keeps its own CRANK_ANGLE and steps it
-- by the same amount: node scripts share no state, so every part works its own pose out from the
-- same crank-slider geometry.
--
-- Clearing the animate mode does not stop the angle where it stands; it runs on to the next top
-- dead centre and parks there. The whole assembly therefore always comes to rest in one known pose,
-- whichever strobe each part happened to see the mode change on.
local STEP = 0.09

local function nextAngle()
    local angle = (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) + STEP
    if angle >= 2 * math.pi then
        angle = 0
    end
    CRANK_ANGLE = angle
    return angle
end

if getStrobe() and (getAnimating() or (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) ~= 0) then
    local angle = nextAngle()
    local c, s = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)

    -- Rotation about Z, in column major order: the crank turns about the main journal axis.
    local t = getTransform()
    t[1] = c; t[2] = s; t[5] = -s; t[6] = c
    setTransform(t)
end

nodes.name: crankGeometry
nodes.coreScript:
-- Face normal taken from the triangle's own winding, so lighting stays correct without any
-- hand-derived normals to keep in step with the geometry.
local function faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local e1x, e1y, e1z = b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2], b[3] - a[3]
    local e2x, e2y, e2z = c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2], c[3] - a[3]
    local nx = e1y * e2z - e1z * e2y
    local ny = e1z * e2x - e1x * e2z
    local nz = e1x * e2y - e1y * e2x
    local len = math.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
    if len < 1e-8 then
        return {0, 1, 0}
    end
    return {nx / len, ny / len, nz / len}
end

local function tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    local n = faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local verts = {
        Vertex{posn = a, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = b, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = c, colour = colour, normal = n},
    }
    if visibility then
        addVertexes(verts, visibility)
    else
        addVertexes(verts)
    end
end

local function quad(a, b, c, d, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, c, d, colour, visibility)
end

-- Axis aligned box between two opposite corners.
local function box(low, high, colour)
    local x0, y0, z0 = low[1], low[2], low[3]
    local x1, y1, z1 = high[1], high[2], high[3]
    quad({x0, y0, z1}, {x1, y0, z1}, {x1, y1, z1}, {x0, y1, z1}, colour)
    quad({x1, y0, z0}, {x0, y0, z0}, {x0, y1, z0}, {x1, y1, z0}, colour)
    quad({x1, y0, z1}, {x1, y0, z0}, {x1, y1, z0}, {x1, y1, z1}, colour)
    quad({x0, y0, z0}, {x0, y0, z1}, {x0, y1, z1}, {x0, y1, z0}, colour)
    quad({x0, y1, z1}, {x1, y1, z1}, {x1, y1, z0}, {x0, y1, z0}, colour)
    quad({x0, y0, z0}, {x1, y0, z0}, {x1, y0, z1}, {x0, y0, z1}, colour)
end

-- Cylinder lying along Z, from z0 to z1 (z1 greater than z0), optionally capped at both ends.
local function cylinderZ(cx, cy, z0, z1, radius, segments, colour, capped)
    local prevX, prevY = cx + radius, cy
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local x, y = cx + radius * math.cos(angle), cy + radius * math.sin(angle)
        quad({prevX, prevY, z0}, {x, y, z0}, {x, y, z1}, {prevX, prevY, z1}, colour)
        if capped then
            tri({cx, cy, z1}, {prevX, prevY, z1}, {x, y, z1}, colour)
            tri({cx, cy, z0}, {x, y, z0}, {prevX, prevY, z0}, colour)
        end
        prevX, prevY = x, y
    end
end

-- Crankshaft, drawn in its own rotating frame: the main journal axis runs along Z through the
-- origin and the crank pin sits one throw away at y = 25, so the whole part turns about the origin.
if vertexCount() == 0 then
    local THROW = 25
    local journal = {140, 148, 160, 255}
    local web = {112, 120, 132, 255}
    local pin = {205, 210, 220, 255}

    -- Main journals, one either side of the throw.
    cylinderZ(0, 0, -52, -26, 11, 20, journal, true)
    cylinderZ(0, 0, 26, 52, 11, 20, journal, true)

    -- Webs carrying the pin, each running past the axis into a counterweight.
    box({-14, -24, -26}, {14, 34, -14}, web)
    box({-14, -24, 14}, {14, 34, 26}, web)

    -- Crank pin, spanning the gap the connecting rod's big end runs in.
    cylinderZ(0, THROW, -15, 15, 9, 20, pin, true)
end

nodes.name: rodPlace
nodes.coreScript:
-- Crank angle in radians, measured from top dead centre, advanced one step per strobe while this
-- node is animating. Each of the three mechanism transforms keeps its own CRANK_ANGLE and steps it
-- by the same amount: node scripts share no state, so every part works its own pose out from the
-- same crank-slider geometry.
--
-- Clearing the animate mode does not stop the angle where it stands; it runs on to the next top
-- dead centre and parks there. The whole assembly therefore always comes to rest in one known pose,
-- whichever strobe each part happened to see the mode change on.
local STEP = 0.09

local function nextAngle()
    local angle = (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) + STEP
    if angle >= 2 * math.pi then
        angle = 0
    end
    CRANK_ANGLE = angle
    return angle
end

-- Crank throw and rod length, the two dimensions the mechanism's geometry is built to.
local THROW = 25
local ROD = 90

if getStrobe() and (getAnimating() or (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) ~= 0) then
    local angle = nextAngle()

    -- Big end rides the crank pin, so this frame is placed on the pin itself. The pin starts at top
    -- dead centre and swings towards -X as the crank turns, matching the crank's own rotation.
    local pinX = -THROW * math.sin(angle)
    local pinY = THROW * math.cos(angle)

    -- The rod leans by however much puts its small end back on the cylinder axis: this frame's own
    -- rotation carries the small end to -ROD * sin(lean), so sin(lean) = pinX / ROD cancels the
    -- offset the big end is sitting at.
    local lean = math.asin(pinX / ROD)
    local c, s = math.cos(lean), math.sin(lean)

    local t = getTransform()
    t[1] = c; t[2] = s; t[5] = -s; t[6] = c
    t[13] = pinX; t[14] = pinY
    setTransform(t)
end

nodes.name: rodGeometry
nodes.coreScript:
-- Face normal taken from the triangle's own winding, so lighting stays correct without any
-- hand-derived normals to keep in step with the geometry.
local function faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local e1x, e1y, e1z = b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2], b[3] - a[3]
    local e2x, e2y, e2z = c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2], c[3] - a[3]
    local nx = e1y * e2z - e1z * e2y
    local ny = e1z * e2x - e1x * e2z
    local nz = e1x * e2y - e1y * e2x
    local len = math.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
    if len < 1e-8 then
        return {0, 1, 0}
    end
    return {nx / len, ny / len, nz / len}
end

local function tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    local n = faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local verts = {
        Vertex{posn = a, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = b, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = c, colour = colour, normal = n},
    }
    if visibility then
        addVertexes(verts, visibility)
    else
        addVertexes(verts)
    end
end

local function quad(a, b, c, d, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, c, d, colour, visibility)
end

-- Bearing boss: a tube lying along Z, walled inside and out and closed by an annulus at each end,
-- so the journal it runs on stays visible through the bore.
local function tubeZ(cx, cy, z0, z1, outer, inner, segments, colour)
    local prevOX, prevOY = cx + outer, cy
    local prevIX, prevIY = cx + inner, cy
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local ca, sa = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
        local ox, oy = cx + outer * ca, cy + outer * sa
        local ix, iy = cx + inner * ca, cy + inner * sa
        quad({prevOX, prevOY, z0}, {ox, oy, z0}, {ox, oy, z1}, {prevOX, prevOY, z1}, colour)
        quad({ix, iy, z0}, {prevIX, prevIY, z0}, {prevIX, prevIY, z1}, {ix, iy, z1}, colour)
        quad({prevIX, prevIY, z1}, {prevOX, prevOY, z1}, {ox, oy, z1}, {ix, iy, z1}, colour)
        quad({prevOX, prevOY, z0}, {prevIX, prevIY, z0}, {ix, iy, z0}, {ox, oy, z0}, colour)
        prevOX, prevOY, prevIX, prevIY = ox, oy, ix, iy
    end
end

-- Connecting rod, drawn along +Y from its big end at the origin to its small end at y = 90, which
-- is the rod length its transform's lean angle is worked out from.
if vertexCount() == 0 then
    local ROD = 90
    local metal = {186, 138, 82, 255}

    -- Big end bore, sized to run on the crank pin, and small end bore, sized to run on the
    -- gudgeon pin.
    tubeZ(0, 0, -14, 14, 17, 9.5, 20, metal)
    tubeZ(0, ROD, -9, 9, 11, 6.5, 16, metal)

    -- Shank, tapering from the big end up to the small end.
    local y0, hx0, hz0 = 6, 9, 5.5
    local y1, hx1, hz1 = 84, 5.5, 4
    quad({hx0, y0, hz0}, {hx0, y0, -hz0}, {hx1, y1, -hz1}, {hx1, y1, hz1}, metal)
    quad({-hx0, y0, -hz0}, {-hx0, y0, hz0}, {-hx1, y1, hz1}, {-hx1, y1, -hz1}, metal)
    quad({-hx0, y0, hz0}, {hx0, y0, hz0}, {hx1, y1, hz1}, {-hx1, y1, hz1}, metal)
    quad({hx0, y0, -hz0}, {-hx0, y0, -hz0}, {-hx1, y1, -hz1}, {hx1, y1, -hz1}, metal)
end

nodes.name: pistonSlide
nodes.coreScript:
-- Crank angle in radians, measured from top dead centre, advanced one step per strobe while this
-- node is animating. Each of the three mechanism transforms keeps its own CRANK_ANGLE and steps it
-- by the same amount: node scripts share no state, so every part works its own pose out from the
-- same crank-slider geometry.
--
-- Clearing the animate mode does not stop the angle where it stands; it runs on to the next top
-- dead centre and parks there. The whole assembly therefore always comes to rest in one known pose,
-- whichever strobe each part happened to see the mode change on.
local STEP = 0.09

local function nextAngle()
    local angle = (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) + STEP
    if angle >= 2 * math.pi then
        angle = 0
    end
    CRANK_ANGLE = angle
    return angle
end

-- Crank throw and rod length, the two dimensions the mechanism's geometry is built to.
local THROW = 25
local ROD = 90

if getStrobe() and (getAnimating() or (CRANK_ANGLE or 0) ~= 0) then
    local angle = nextAngle()

    -- Gudgeon pin height for this crank angle: the crank pin's own height plus the vertical reach
    -- of the leaning rod. Slides along Y only, so the piston never leaves the cylinder axis.
    local offset = -THROW * math.sin(angle)
    local height = THROW * math.cos(angle) + math.sqrt(ROD * ROD - offset * offset)

    local t = getTransform()
    t[14] = height
    setTransform(t)
end

    local e2x, e2y, e2z = c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2], c[3] - a[3]

local function quad(a, b, c, d, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, c, d, colour, visibility)
end

-- Cylinder standing along Y, from y0 to y1 (y1 greater than y0), capped at either end on request.
local function cylinderY(cx, cz, y0, y1, radius, segments, colour, capTop, capBottom)
    local prevX, prevZ = cx + radius, cz
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local x, z = cx + radius * math.cos(angle), cz + radius * math.sin(angle)
        quad({prevX, y0, prevZ}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, {x, y1, z}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        if capTop then
            tri({cx, y1, cz}, {x, y1, z}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, colour)
        end
        if capBottom then
            tri({cx, y0, cz}, {prevX, y0, prevZ}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        end
        prevX, prevZ = x, z
    end
end

-- Cylinder lying along Z, from z0 to z1 (z1 greater than z0), optionally capped at both ends.
local function cylinderZ(cx, cy, z0, z1, radius, segments, colour, capped)
    local prevX, prevY = cx + radius, cy
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local x, y = cx + radius * math.cos(angle), cy + radius * math.sin(angle)
        quad({prevX, prevY, z0}, {x, y, z0}, {x, y, z1}, {prevX, prevY, z1}, colour)
        if capped then
            tri({cx, cy, z1}, {prevX, prevY, z1}, {x, y, z1}, colour)
            tri({cx, cy, z0}, {x, y, z0}, {prevX, prevY, z0}, colour)
        end
        prevX, prevY = x, y
    end
end

-- Piston, drawn about its gudgeon pin at the origin, which is where the connecting rod's small end
-- reaches: its transform only ever slides it along Y, so this frame stays upright.
if vertexCount() == 0 then
    local alloy = {206, 210, 216, 255}
    local ring = {70, 72, 78, 255}
    local steel = {96, 102, 112, 255}

    -- Crown and skirt, closed at both ends.
    cylinderY(0, 0, -24, 26, 22, 24, alloy, true, true)

    -- Compression rings, standing just proud of the skirt.
    cylinderY(0, 0, 14, 17, 22.6, 24, ring, false, false)
    cylinderY(0, 0, 8, 11, 22.6, 24, ring, false, false)

    -- Gudgeon pin, its ends left showing where the rod's small end is hidden inside the skirt.
    cylinderZ(0, 0, -24, 24, 6.5, 16, steel, true)
end

-- hand-derived normals to keep in step with the geometry.
local function faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local e1x, e1y, e1z = b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2], b[3] - a[3]
    local e2x, e2y, e2z = c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2], c[3] - a[3]
    local nx = e1y * e2z - e1z * e2y
    local ny = e1z * e2x - e1x * e2z
    local nz = e1x * e2y - e1y * e2x

    if len < 1e-8 then
        return {0, 1, 0}
    end
    return {nx / len, ny / len, nz / len}

local function tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    local n = faceNormal(a, b, c)
    local verts = {
        Vertex{posn = a, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = b, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = c, colour = colour, normal = n},
    }
    if visibility then
        addVertexes(verts, visibility)
    else
        addVertexes(verts)
    end
end

local function quad(a, b, c, d, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, c, d, colour, visibility)
end

-- Cylinder standing along Y, from y0 to y1 (y1 greater than y0), capped at either end on request.
local function cylinderY(cx, cz, y0, y1, radius, segments, colour, capTop, capBottom)
    local prevX, prevZ = cx + radius, cz
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local x, z = cx + radius * math.cos(angle), cz + radius * math.sin(angle)
        quad({prevX, y0, prevZ}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, {x, y1, z}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        if capTop then
            tri({cx, y1, cz}, {x, y1, z}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, colour)
        end
        if capBottom then
            tri({cx, y0, cz}, {prevX, y0, prevZ}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        end
        prevX, prevZ = x, z
    end
end

-- Flat annulus lying in the XZ plane, facing up.
local function ringY(y, inner, outer, segments, colour, visibility)
    local prevIX, prevIZ = inner, 0
    local prevOX, prevOZ = outer, 0
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local ca, sa = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
        local ix, iz = inner * ca, inner * sa
        local ox, oz = outer * ca, outer * sa
        quad({prevIX, y, prevIZ}, {ix, y, iz}, {ox, y, oz}, {prevOX, y, prevOZ}, colour, visibility)
        prevIX, prevIZ, prevOX, prevOZ = ix, iz, ox, oz
    end
end

-- Plinth the button stands on, plus a ring that lights up while the engine is running. The ring is
-- AGENT visibility geometry driven from here rather than by an agent: setAgentVisible() is the one
-- switch a script has over whether a vertex group is drawn, so it serves as the running lamp.
if vertexCount() == 0 then
    cylinderY(0, 0, -5, 0, 16, 28, {58, 62, 70, 255}, true, true)
    ringY(0.5, 17, 21, 28, {60, 220, 120, 150}, VertexVisibility.AGENT)
end

-- The animate mode reaches this node on the action the button emits, so the lamp tracks the engine.
setAgentVisible(getAnimating())

nodes.name: buttonLift
nodes.coreScript:
-- Rides the button down while the engine runs and lets it spring back when it stops. This node
-- follows the animate mode rather than the poke, so the cap shows what the assembly is doing.
local DEPRESSED = -3
local EASE = 0.35

if getStrobe() then
    local t = getTransform()
    local target = getAnimating() and DEPRESSED or 0
    local y = t[14] + (target - t[14]) * EASE

    if math.abs(target - y) < 0.05 then
        y = target
    end

    if y ~= t[14] then
        t[14] = y
        setTransform(t)
    end
end

    local e2x, e2y, e2z = c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2], c[3] - a[3]

    end

    local verts = {
        Vertex{posn = a, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = b, colour = colour, normal = n},
        Vertex{posn = c, colour = colour, normal = n},
    }
    if visibility then
        addVertexes(verts, visibility)
    else
        addVertexes(verts)
    end
end

local function quad(a, b, c, d, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, b, c, colour, visibility)
    tri(a, c, d, colour, visibility)
end

-- Cylinder standing along Y, from y0 to y1 (y1 greater than y0), capped at either end on request.
local function cylinderY(cx, cz, y0, y1, radius, segments, colour, capTop, capBottom)
    local prevX, prevZ = cx + radius, cz
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local x, z = cx + radius * math.cos(angle), cz + radius * math.sin(angle)
        quad({prevX, y0, prevZ}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, {x, y1, z}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        if capTop then
            tri({cx, y1, cz}, {x, y1, z}, {prevX, y1, prevZ}, colour)
        end
        if capBottom then
            tri({cx, y0, cz}, {prevX, y0, prevZ}, {x, y0, z}, colour)
        end
        prevX, prevZ = x, z
    end
end

-- Dome standing on a circular base of the same radius: rings of an ellipsoid cap, vertical at the
-- rim so it meets a cylinder of that radius without a seam, and closed by a fan at the apex.
local function domeY(y, radius, height, segments, rings, colour)
    local function ringRadius(level) return radius * math.cos((level / rings) * (math.pi / 2)) end
    local function ringHeight(level) return y + height * math.sin((level / rings) * (math.pi / 2)) end

    for level = 0, rings - 1 do
        local r0, y0 = ringRadius(level), ringHeight(level)
        local r1, y1 = ringRadius(level + 1), ringHeight(level + 1)
        local prevX0, prevZ0 = r0, 0
        local prevX1, prevZ1 = r1, 0

        for i = 1, segments do
            local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
            local ca, sa = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
            local x0, z0 = r0 * ca, r0 * sa
            local x1, z1 = r1 * ca, r1 * sa

            if level == rings - 1 then
                tri({prevX0, y0, prevZ0}, {0, y1, 0}, {x0, y0, z0}, colour)
            else
                quad({prevX0, y0, prevZ0}, {prevX1, y1, prevZ1}, {x1, y1, z1}, {x0, y0, z0}, colour)
            end

            prevX0, prevZ0 = x0, z0
            prevX1, prevZ1 = x1, z1
        end
    end
end

-- Flat annulus lying in the XZ plane, facing up.
local function ringY(y, inner, outer, segments, colour, visibility)
    local prevIX, prevIZ = inner, 0
    local prevOX, prevOZ = outer, 0
    for i = 1, segments do
        local angle = (i / segments) * 2 * math.pi
        local ca, sa = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
        local ix, iz = inner * ca, inner * sa
        local ox, oz = outer * ca, outer * sa
        quad({prevIX, y, prevIZ}, {ix, y, iz}, {ox, y, oz}, {prevOX, y, prevOZ}, colour, visibility)
        prevIX, prevIZ, prevOX, prevOZ = ix, iz, ox, oz
    end
end

-- The button itself: a short skirt closed by a domed top, left uncapped where the dome sits on it.
-- Hovering the pointer over it brings up a halo; hitting it runs the pokeScript.
if vertexCount() == 0 then
    local red = {198, 62, 48, 255}

    cylinderY(0, 0, 0.5, 4.5, 10, 28, red, false, true)
    domeY(4.5, 10, 3, 28, 4, red)
    ringY(7.5, 10.5, 13.5, 28, {90, 160, 220, 110}, VertexVisibility.HOVERED_OVER)
end
